newsitem.title: USA: Clinton proposes to renew Superfund taxes.
newsitem.headline: Clinton proposes to renew Superfund taxes.

text.p: The Clinton administration Thursday proposed to reinstate oil, chemical, and corporate environmental taxes to help fill the Superfund trust fund.
The White House's budget plan for 1998 through 2002 envisioned the oil and chemical excise taxes yielding a total of $700 million annually beginning in the 1998 fiscal year.
It saw the corporate environmental tax raising $1.1 billion in 1998, $700 million in 1999, and $800 million annually in the following three years.
The taxes, which are used to help pay for cleanups at the nation's worst toxic waste sites, expired at the end of 1995.
Republicans last year refused to renew the taxes until Congress had agreed to overhaul the Superfund program to speed up and cut the cost of cleanups.

Proposals to change the program failed to advance as Republicans battled with the administration over plans to relieve companies from paying for cleanups at sites where they dumped waste legally before 1981.

The Congressional Budget Office last year estimated that that the Superfund trust fund, which helps cover cleanup costs at sites where liable parties cannot be found or cannot pay, would run out of money by 2000 if the taxes were not renewed.
